items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...they had great soloists — Charlie Mariano, Lenny Niehaus, Frank Rosolino and Carl Fontana and there was a lot of good soloists on the band.

ctx.x: How does Kenton fit into the jazz history, as far as you guys are concerned?

Well I mean I liked the man, he was a great man. I thought he treated people right. But I wouldn’t say he was a jazz musician. He just liked anything that was progressive and interesting. And as you can tell from his music, there was some very interesting things played but they were nowhere near jazz, like “City of Glass” and all of these things were really far out for the time you know. And as close as he got to jazz was in ‘55 the band © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

we had in 1955 where Bill Holman was writing. and then it started to lean towards the swing/ jazz thing and they had great soloists — Charlie Mariano, Lenny Niehaus, Frank Rosolino and Carl Fontana and there was a lot of good soloists on the band. And then the band leaned a little bit more toward jazz. But actually, Stan wasn’t really a jazz kind of person or musician. He just wanted interesting music. And it leaned toward jazz.
